_doc: Service life of a durable good: the years a stock of it serves before it is worn out or lost, so households hold it and buy only to keep it up (the economy reads a good with a service life as a durable; a good not listed is used up within the year). Keyed by the good ids of data/production. Estimates, confidence C or D; a wear model per good (use, material, maintenance) would derive them. Carts and ships are not goods in the production data yet, so they have no entry; timber, cloth and other materials that are also consumed as inputs are left out until a held-stock model separates the two uses.

brick_1000.source: Fired-brick walls stand for generations when roofed and repaired; taken as most of a lifetime or more. Estimate.

stone_blocks.source: Dressed-stone walls outlast brick; Roman and medieval masonry buildings still stand. Estimate of the time to rebuild.

cement_portland_kg.source: Design working life of building structures, 50 years, in EN 1990 (Eurocode: Basis of structural design), table 2.1 category 4.

bronze_kg.source: Working life of a hand tool, blade or fitting before wear, breakage or loss replaces it; harder metals outlast softer, cutting edges wear fastest. Estimate.
